review_round.register: P0/P1/P2 EXACT FIX ACTION REGISTER - REVISED

pin_policy: Every SHA/version quoted in any WWHN-290 markdown artifact MUST equal the value recorded here. Wwhn290ClosureEvidenceTest enforces cross-document equality so a hand-copied pin can never rot silently again.

frozen_candidate.policy: The closure package is frozen by a fixed commit plus a content digest. The digest is a sha256 over the manifest of 'sha256(file)  path' lines, sorted by path, computed from the frozen commit's own git objects. Later commits on the shared m1 branch therefore cannot rot it, which is the failure mode that made the revision-1 blob pin worthless within hours.
frozen_candidate.sha_note: Written by the evidence-only commit that immediately follows the freeze commit: a commit can never contain its own hash.
frozen_candidate.excluded_note: The pins file holds the digest and cannot contain it; the gate-run record and raw logs are append-only run evidence written after the freeze.

branch_decision.decision: m1 is the canonical BE implementation and closure source for WWHN-290
branch_decision.effective_sha_note: Equals frozen_candidate.sha; written by the same evidence-only commit.
branch_decision.port_option_rejected_because: merge-base(m1, m1-be-2) equals the m1-be-2 HEAD, so a port/merge is a no-op and would create a second, older copy of the closure source.

superseded_branch.name: m1-be-2
superseded_branch.head: 60816499066f9f493596e326dc41116ef32f5c4b
superseded_branch.m1_commits_ahead_note: Deliberately not pinned: m1 is shared and this number grows daily; the invariant that matters is behind = 0. The verifier prints the live value.
superseded_branch.rationale: merge-base(m1, m1-be-2) equals the m1-be-2 HEAD itself, therefore m1 already contains every m1-be-2 commit. There is no divergence to reconcile and no closure source to port.

change_range.attribution_note: m1 is shared and WWHN-290 commits are interleaved with other tickets, so the data-impact claim is verified TWICE: over the contiguous base..final range, and per attributed commit. The commits list is the authoritative set of WWHN-290-attributed commits on m1; each is checked individually for guarded-path changes so an unrelated ticket landing in between can never dilute or inflate this ticket claim.

contract.lineage_note: The approved contract TARGET for WWHN-290 is info.version 2.0.0 and it is asserted live against the working tree. The blob identity above is the observed value at pin time ONLY and is deliberately not treated as a closure assertion. m1 is a shared branch and the contract file is regenerated by other tickets: WWHN-328 moved it from c262a0d3 to 50b81fd5 to publish dashboard data-scope fields, and it moved again within the same day, each time keeping info.version at 2.0.0. WWHN-290 therefore pins a RANGE INVARIANT - its own commit range changes the contract file zero times, which stays true forever - instead of an absolute blob that any concurrent ticket rots within hours.

ba_document_contract.note: Requirement layer owned by BA. It does not compete with the generated implementation contract; mixing the two layers is what produced the 1.0.0 vs 2.0.0 argument in the review.

contract_consumers.namespace_exception_note: The platform health endpoint sits outside the versioned business namespace by design and the FE declares it separately through VITE_API_HEALTH_PATH.
historical_not_closure_evidence: storage/api-docs/api-docs.json@m1-be-2 (info.version 1.0.0, ancestor revision of the same file)

fe_consumer.note: Round 2 pinned 3ddce52 as the reviewed FE revision. Round 3 moves the pin forward to the FE commit that actually carries the FE consumer confirmation document, so the pinned revision and the evidence it is supposed to contain can never disagree.
